summary: Integrated arity/compression indexing, spectral-vs-chronological separation, multimodal synchronous-state harmonics, projection-bounded inference, covariance/cycle-consistency tests, and relay registry bindings.

key_findings: Egyptian and cuneiform independently increase phonetic explicitness as writing takes on broader linguistic burden.
Ugarit holds material technology relatively constant while changing encoding granularity.
Root arity and sign arity must remain independent.
Indo-European root enlargement provides an independent mechanism control, not proof of Semitic derivation.
Ancient scribal crosswalks should calibrate uncertain transformations before speculative projection.

summary: Integrated the supplied Byblos sign chart and multilingual-inscription survey into the recursive calibration architecture.
findings: Byblos is promoted as a negative decipherment control: small corpus, uncertain sign normalization, unknown language, no secure explicit crosswalk.
The uploaded chart supplies sign IDs, strongly skewed token frequencies, medium metadata, and explicit variant series without supplying phonetic values.
Ugarit is promoted from a single KTU 5.14 crosswalk to a multilingual archive hub with intersecting bilingual/trilingual/quadrilingual paths.
Crosswalk degree, anchor density, crosswalk depth, decipherment entropy and value-assignment entropy are now first-class variables.
A holdout-decipherment test is required before any proposed Byblos sign-value system can be promoted.
A survey-derived benchmark registry now pairs successful multilingual decipherment cases with Byblos as a negative control.
